title: Nervonic acid in WWOX-LoF
summary: A conditional tracer for very-long-chain myelin lipid production and delivery.

graph.evidence: WWOX mouse lipid-pathway and myelin RNA fall together.
graph.inference: Precursor, synthesis and delivery are separable.
graph.hypothesis: An upstream deficit may respond if downstream steps are intact.
graph.experiment: Trace intact C24:1 to absolute sheath lipid and conduction.

evidence: In CerS2-deficient brain, C24:1 and C24:0 GalCer both fell to about 3% of control, while their mean within-mouse ratio rose. In GLTP-deficient myelin, a HexCer 42:2 signal fell to 58% at P14.
inference: The ratio can hide loss of both C24 species. A separate lipid delivery defect can reduce sheath lipid too. WWOX mouse and human organoid CERS2 RNA have opposite directions.
hypothesis: Nervonic acid could bypass poor elongation when acyl incorporation and delivery still work. Product formation could remain limited by oligodendrocyte state, or lipid may fail to reach eligible axons.
experiment: At matched local labeled precursor, quantify intact C24:1 acyl-CoA, absolute GalCer and sulfatide in cells and myelin, persistent first sheaths and conduction.
limits: Oral acid lowered brain C26:0-LPC in Abcd1 mice by about 56% without a detected C24:1 increase. Pediatric local exposure and safety remain open. Retain for tracing and defer WWOX trial priority.
